handoff: Review approved: one waitForTickLock helper covers every person command; B1–B16 traced (table in handoff); typecheck, unit tier and tick-lock-wait/story-wait/machine-dir/migrate integration green. Three non-blocking points (B10 second command never waits, B8 fake pid, duplicated time formatting).

findings.title: B10's second command never waits
findings.detail:
The B10 test starts the second tidy after releasing the lock, so it runs at once; only the first command's holder change (D6) is exercised. B10 says 'norn tidy started meanwhile prints the wait line and runs when the edit finishes'. The code path is the same helper, so behaviour is covered by construction.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Optionally start the second command while the first holds the lock and assert its wait line.

findings.title: B8 uses a made-up pid instead of a reaped process
findings.detail:
Testing decisions say 'B8 uses a real reaped process'; the test writes pid 999999. Effective, but could collide with a live pid on some machine.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Spawn and reap a process and use its pid.

findings.title: Local-time HH:MM:SS formatting duplicated
findings.detail:
holderText formats with new Date(at).toTimeString().slice(0, 8), the same as watch.ts clockTime.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Share one helper.
